paragraphs.text: Lake Kessel disappeared from maps in 1961, when a canal drained it to create farmland. The soil turned out to be poor, and within twenty years most of the fields had been abandoned.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: In 2004 a group of farmers and biologists proposed letting the water return. Local opinion was divided: some feared mosquitoes and lost land, others hoped for tourism and better hunting.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The canal was closed in 2009, and the lake filled within three winters. Today it draws birdwatchers from across the country, although two families still farm the drier northern edge.
paragraphs.label: C
